title: Inserting an element: temporary storage, right shift, and write-back
summary: First save the trailing 3, then copy 5 and 4 one position to the right, and finally write 3 to index 3.
context: The input array is nums = [1, 1, 2, 4, 5, 3] (indices 0 through 5), where the first five elements on the left, [1, 1, 2, 4, 5], are already sorted, and the task is to "Insert element 3 into its correct position in the sorted region of nums" (index 3, between elements 2 and 4).
description: First store the trailing 3 temporarily in base so it will not be overwritten during shifting. Copy the elements greater than 3—namely 5 and then 4—one position to the right; these assignments temporarily leave two 5s or two 4s in the array.

Stop shifting right once comparison reaches value 2 at index 2, and write base to index 3. In the figure, the left side keeps a fixed snapshot of the input while the four rows on the right show the successive changes; the four rows in the table below correspond to those four states on the right, with row 1 still showing the initial array.

frames.title: Inserting an element: temporary storage, right shift, and write-back
frames.explanation: The two right shifts are copy assignments; the element 3 to be inserted is held in base throughout and finally written back into the vacated insertion position.

prose.title: Inserting an element: temporary storage, right shift, and write-back
prose.summary: Four steps show temporary storage, two right-shift copies, and write-back; each step's table lists the actual contents of nums at that moment.

steps.title: Temporarily store the trailing 3
steps.explanation: First save element 3 at the final index 5—the element to be inserted—into variable base = 3 so it will not be lost when overwritten by subsequent right shifts; the array contents have not changed yet.
steps.key_state: 3 is stored in base; nums is still [1, 1, 2, 4, 5, 3].
steps.announcement: Stored element 3 in base for insertion.

steps.title: Copy 5 to index 5
steps.explanation: Compare 5 at index 4: because 5 is greater than base (3), execute the assignment nums[5] = nums[4] to copy 5 right to index 5, temporarily leaving two 5s in the array; the original trailing 3 is preserved in base and not lost.
steps.key_state: 5 is copied to index 5, so nums = [1, 1, 2, 4, 5, 5], with both indices 4 and 5 holding 5; base remains 3.
steps.announcement: Copied 5 to index 5; 3 remains stored in base.

steps.title: Copy 4 to index 4
steps.explanation: Continue left to compare 4 at index 3: because 4 is also greater than base (3), execute the assignment nums[4] = nums[3] to copy 4 right to index 4, overwriting the extra 5 and temporarily leaving two 4s in the array; base remains 3.
steps.key_state: 4 is copied to index 4, so nums = [1, 1, 2, 4, 4, 5], with both indices 3 and 4 holding 4; base remains 3.
steps.announcement: Copied 4 to index 4; 3 remains stored in base.

steps.title: Write 3 to index 3
steps.explanation: Continue left to compare 2 at index 2: because 2 is not greater than base (3), stop shifting right and execute nums[3] = base to write the stored 3 to index 3, replacing the duplicate 4 and completing this insertion. All six elements are now in ascending order, and the two existing 1s remain unchanged.
steps.key_state: 3 from base is written to index 3, so nums = [1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5], completing this insertion.
